Hi Irene,

We're moving the Metrics Pipeline connector through procurement and noticed the SOC 2 Type II package you provided lists an audit period that ended 2026-09-30. Our procurement policy requires an auditor-signed report covering the last 12 months or an auditor-issued bridge/interim attestation that explicitly covers the gap.

- Provide a reissued Type II with an updated audit period, or
- Provide an auditor-signed interim attestation (or bridge letter) that covers 2026-10-01 to the present

If a reissue is not possible within our procurement timeline, an interim attestation signed by an appropriate security executive plus a written note from your auditor confirming scope would be acceptable. Please include expected delivery timelines and any files you can share now.

We need the documents uploaded to our procurement portal by 2026-11-05 to keep the contract on schedule.

What we can provide this week:
- Draft interim attestation (company-signed) covering 2026-10-01 through 2026-11-30 — draft attached.
- A written confirmation from our independent auditor (Crowne & Partners) confirming the control scope for the attestation and that the gap is covered by the attestation instrument (we have an auditor contact who has agreed to provide an email confirmation by 2026-11-04).

Proposed timeline:
- 2026-11-03: Deliver draft interim attestation to you for procurement/legal review (DOCX attached).
- 2026-11-04: Auditor confirmation email to procurement/legal.
- 2026-11-06: Final signed attestation and upload to your portal (we can also provide a DocuSign envelope).

If ACME's procurement policy requires the auditor to sign the attestation directly, please let us know and we'll prioritize elevating the request. Otherwise, the combination of a signed interim attestation from Redwood's Head of Security plus the auditor email is typically accepted by larger customers.

Action items for us: Ben and Grace — can you confirm the legal language and whether we should route the attestation through DocuSign (preferred) or attach a signed PDF?

Best,

Irene — thanks for the quick reply and proposed timeline. A few clarifying points from legal/procurement:
- Procurement requires an auditor-signed statement when the contiguous 12-month Type II window ends within the last 90 days of award.
- If the auditor is unable to sign an attestation, procurement will accept a signed company attestation plus an email from the auditor confirming their review and that the attestation follows the same scope.

We'd prefer the auditor-signed option if you can accelerate it, but the combination you outlined (signed interim + auditor email) is acceptable. Please ensure the auditor email includes their firm letterhead and contact info.

Also — when you share the draft on 11/03, could you add a one-paragraph summary of what changed relative to the last report (controls in-scope, exceptions, if any)? That helps legal triage faster.
